question: Does the compiled private Codex interaction bridge hold native command approvals as authority-owned pending state, write exactly one host-chosen native decision or a decision-free error, keep delivery unknown and never resend, while interrupt, expiry, transport loss and process exit behave as the bridge claims?

scenarios.N1: a not-offered decline refused locally, then native cancel and a duplicate reply
scenarios.N3: traffic and an independent session while an approval is held
scenarios.N4: interrupt while an approval is held
scenarios.N5: SIGKILL while an approval is held, then resume on a fresh app-server
scenarios.N7: interrupt while an accepted command runs

pinnedFields: N1 choices, item status, terminal, inference and server-request id types and offered decisions; N2 terminal, item, marker and inference; N3 concurrent requests and A terminal; N4 terminal within 5 s, terminal, settlements, item and inference; N5 completion, resumed last turn and items, server requests after resume and replayed pending; N7 command started, terminal, item and marker; N8 advertised candidates and reactions; N9 terminal within 5 s, terminal and item. Outcomes, statuses, counts and booleans only: no ID, path, timestamp or hash. Native notification order (report.order) and N4 withdrawnBy, which follows it, are recorded but not pinned: resolved, item and turn notifications come from separate native sources, and 0.169 cross-source order already varied (execution X1 thread/started). Once outcome is non-null, interaction-proof.mjs fails on any other pinned value.

native.detail: Recorded from identical pinned objects on linux/arm64 (coordinator, local) and linux/x64 (CI, outcome null, report only) at da20172, with harness and N1-N5, N7-N9 true on both; the pin audit then removed the order fields from both alike. Natively observed on both: every command approval offers [accept, {acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment}, cancel] with a numeric id and no approvalId; cancel leaves the item declined and the turn interrupted after one inference; accept runs the command (marker written) and completes after a second inference; interrupt while held ends the turn interrupted within 5 s with no command item, withdrawing the approval; SIGKILL while held leaves the turn unconcluded and resume shows the last turn interrupted with no command item, no server request and no replayed approval; interrupt while an accepted sleep 3 runs ends the turn interrupted with no command item and no marker; request_user_input is advertised but its call reaches no client: with the fixture marker fixed (x64 CI run 44220562636, job 134521071264, at 069b309; every other pinned value identical) the call and its continuation are two inferences, no server request arrives and the turn completes with a user and an agent message; a host expiry -32000 fails the command item and the turn completes. CI reruns x64 against this pin on every head, and arm64 is rerun by the coordinator.

n8MarkerFix.head: 069b309
n8MarkerFix.detail: At da20172 the fixture marker pattern dropped _, so N8 never called request_user_input (inference 0 on both architectures). With the fix, x64 differs from the da20172 pin only in N8.reactions.request_user_input.inference (0 to 2); the coordinator reruns arm64 on the final head.

scope: Synthetic Linux homes and a loopback Responses service only. Not macOS, live providers, file-change, permission, user-input, elicitation or dynamic-tool requests unless N8 finds them advertised, or cross-process admission.
